mappings.note: All three parts are plant body organisation -- Spirogyra's cell structure, thallus against a differentiated vascular body, and the bryophyte's incomplete move to land -- so one content code, C4.2, plus LO-27 for the explicit drawing instruction in (a).

Porifera against Cnidaria, then the advantage the cnidarian's specialised cells confer: LO-6 covers both halves, since it is written as the tissue level in Cnidaria contrasted with the cellular level in Porifera. No second code needed -- the item never leaves that one contrast.

POOR FIT on content: the full seven-rank hierarchy, drawn and explained, with the largest group and the most-shared-features group named -- and curriculum 82 has no rank outcome. LO-27 is genuinely earned by the labelled-diagram instruction; C-4.1-LO-2 is a stand-in cited on its 'classify organisms in groups' clause.

Part (b) asks outright why angiosperms are the most successful group, which is adaptive structure and function (C4.5); part (a) is the naked-against-enclosed seed contrast, which has no outcome of its own and falls back to C4.2. The clearest case in the chapter of the missing plant-reproduction outcome.

Part (a) names the features that mark Arthropoda (LO-5's placement work); part (b) argues the exoskeleton's advantage over soft-bodied molluscs (C4.5). NOT C4.2-LO-8 despite Mollusca being named: the molluscs appear only as 'soft-bodied' foils and none of the organ systems LO-8 describes are discussed.

The notochord as the criterion that splits the animal kingdom (LO-5) and then the invertebrate-to-vertebrate transition read through protochordates (C4.5). Part (b)'s explicit 'evolutionary transition' wording is what earns the second code here, where the short notochord items take LO-5 alone.

Part (a) places two organisms in kingdoms, Protista and Fungi (C-4.1-LO-2); part (b) asks for the structural characteristics that justify the placement, which is C-4.1-LO-1. The two-part structure is exactly the LO-2 then LO-1 division used throughout this map.

Western Ghats case study: the hotspot criterion and the extinction risk from habitat loss are the conservation argument (C5.2), while the opening ask, the term for species restricted to one region, is endemism as distribution (C2.8). Both halves are separately marked.

Reena's three sorting steps are C-4.1-LO-1's three characteristics in order -- cell number, cell wall, mode of nutrition -- and part (a), the advantage of classifying at all, is C-4.1-LO-2's grouping. Not the rank hierarchy: no taxonomic level is named anywhere in the item.

Two kingdoms placed from a biogas plant and a ditch (C-4.1-LO-2), with the prokaryote-against-eukaryote contrast that justifies both (C-4.1-LO-1). Not C6.1: the biogas plant here belongs to an unnamed farmer, unlike the Ram Bux Singh item, which is about India's contribution.

Parts (a) and (b) place the bracket fungi in Fungi and name their saprophytic role -- kingdom plus ecological role, C-4.1-LO-2 -- while (c) and (d) are the lichen partnership and its use as a pollution indicator, which is LO-15, the row that names lichens.

Mosses against ferns on vascular tissue, true roots and the structures bryophytes only approximate -- plant body organisation throughout, C4.2. The amphibian label in (a) is explained from the same body plan, so no second code is added.

Part (b) asks how needle leaves help in a harsh dry climate, which is adaptation (C4.5); parts (a) and (c) place the trees in gymnosperms and angiosperms by cones against flowers and fruits, which has no plant-division outcome and falls back to C4.2.

Four parts on three rows: the ringed burrowing animal is identified as Annelida from its segments (LO-7), the jointed-legged one as Arthropoda from its appendages and body regions (LO-5), and (d) asks what the exoskeleton does for it (C4.5). All three earn their place; three is the cap.

Parts (a) and (b) are the system, its author and the meaning of each word -- LO-3's rules and significance -- while (c), choosing Panthera for a newly found cat on shared features, is LO-4 applying the system to a real organism. The one item in the chapter that clearly needs both nomenclature rows.

Part (a) is settled by reading Canis familiaris against Canis lupus, which is binomial nomenclature applied (LO-4). Part (b), whether Phylum Chordata or Class Mammalia is broader, is rank hierarchy and a POOR FIT -- no outcome covers ranks, so C-4.1-LO-2 stands in on its grouping clause.

Three genuinely different asks: agricultural runoff and dams threatening the lake, with conservation measures following (C5.2); the phumdis as a habitat and what altering water levels does to it (C2.8); and the Sangai's hooves as an adaptation to spongy floating ground (C4.5). Three codes, one per part.
